name: Generalized keyframes + Cascade (ADR-0035)
description:
## Goal
Implement ADR-0035 (docs/adr/0035-generalized-keyframes-and-cascade.md), grilled + written 2026-07-01. Ordered per-channel keyframes[] + per-property ease (constrained enum) + Cascade (ms-offset enter anchoring). Epic #1 of the capability arc.

## Decisions (all locked in the ADR)
- Ownership REPLACE: keyframes on an element bypass the pipeline's intrinsic motion-form; no keyframes → today's render byte-for-byte.
- Channels v1: overlay opacity/x/y/scale/rotation; surface opacity only. Absorbs overlay-rotation task 5vcak6og.
- Cascade: overlays + marks + textAnimations anchor enter to another element's enter start|end + offsetMs (ms, not fraction — welded through re-times); topo-sort at manifest build; cycles = lint error.
- keyframe.atMs is ms from resolved clip start; ease is INTO the keyframe.
- enter/exit stays as lossless sugar (byte-identical round-trip gate); getEaseGsap opacity-exit special case deleted.
- Rubric: lint the derived enter envelope; inside = Critic taste.
- Sound cues resolve after cascade (welded re-times).

## Order
schema (26apzdha) → manifest builder (6wkaxbis) → {sound re-ground (o9umex5a), timeline GUI (xswyxxwi), inspector GUI (43qu70in), reference piece + rubric (qme17y7z)}.

## Done when
Reference deliverable Critic-ACCEPTed; existing corpus pixel-identical; round-trip test green; GUI proof screenshots captured.

name: Restore signal lights to state-only roles on home (F-03)
description:
## What
Signal lights used decoratively: section headings color-coded (cyan=Your compositions, yellow=Starter templates, red=Demos and fixtures), .home__new CTA is a yellow FILL turning cyan on hover, card hover shows a cyan ring. DESIGN.md: yellow=selection only (never a fill behind text), cyan=time only, red=danger only.

## Why
The one-meaning color grammar is the identity's anchor; the home screen — first thing seen — teaches the wrong grammar before the editor teaches the right one.

## How
Headings → monochrome muted #8A8A90 caps (spec section-label). New composition → quiet raised-step button (#1A1A1D bg, #E8E8EA label); if it needs primary-action emphasis, a 1px yellow BORDER stays within the selection grammar. Hovers → lighter-neutral border shift, never cyan. Evidence: measured heading colors rgb(45,232,238)/rgb(255,214,8)/rgb(230,50,42); button bg rgb(255,214,8); hover capture shows cyan ring on non-selected card.

## Done when
On the homepage, yellow appears only as selection/focus indication, cyan not at all (no playhead here), red not at all (no destructive surface except delete affordances) — verified by screenshot sweep.

name: Reference backdrop behind canvas — judge overlays over real footage (ADR-0034 §7)
description:
GAP — speced in ADR-0034 §7, no task, no code. §7: transparent overlays render over a dark checkerboard by default, WITH an optional reference still / clip backdrop so an overlay is judged over real footage as it'll actually be used. Only the checkerboard exists. This matters for the core use case — you cannot evaluate an overlay's legibility/contrast over a checkerboard.

ASSETS: Scott will drop reference stills into static/backdrops/ (real channel footage — talking-head, gameplay, slides). Build the picker to enumerate whatever is in that folder (Vite serves static/ at /). Do NOT hardcode a fixed asset list — read the folder so adding a still later just works. If the folder is empty at build time, the toggle still works (degrades to checkerboard) and shows nothing to pick.

Build a backdrop toggle/picker in the canvas-framing cluster (next to checkerboard) that places the selected reference image BEHIND the transparent composition in VideoFrame — purely a preview aid, never part of the composition or the export (export keys off the composition's own backgroundFill, not this). The backdrop sits under the WebGPU canvas (premultiplied-alpha transparent) so the overlay composites over it visually. Checkerboard off when a backdrop is shown. Picker UI lives in the controls bar per §7. Apply ux-interface-design + design-engineering.

DONE: drop a still in static/backdrops/, toggle it on, a transparent overlay (e.g. lower-third) is visibly composited over it in the canvas; backdrop never affects export. Chrome screenshot proof (overlay over a reference still) required before close.
result: Reference backdrop behind canvas shipped (ADR-0034 §7). /api/backdrops enumerates static/backdrops/ per-request (no hardcoded list, mtime-versioned URLs so replaced stills never serve stale cache). Picker popover in the canvas-framing cluster (duotone image icon Scott supplied) with live thumbnails, #ffd608 active ring, click-again-to-deselect, light dismiss. Backdrop renders as cover-cropped under the premultiplied-alpha transparent WebGPU canvas in VideoFrame; checkerboard suppressed while active; clicking checkerboard clears backdrop. Verified in Chrome with real channel footage: lower-third composited over screen.png (docs/critic-captures/backdrop-final-proof.png, backdrop-final-new-icon.png), vertical reflow cover-crop, empty-folder degradation to checkerboard, fresh enumeration without reload (Scott's still appeared live mid-session). name: Manifest builder: keyframe + cascade tween emission
description:
ADR-0035 §2/§4. Workspace.svelte buildAnimationManifest (~306-420):
1. Topo-sort cascade anchors → absolute starts (ms→fraction against transport.durationSeconds) BEFORE tween emission; cycles already rejected by lint but assert here too.
2. Elements WITHOUT channels: unchanged path (sugar → visibility fraction → intrinsic motion-form) — zero visual change to existing corpus is the acceptance bar.
3. Elements WITH channels: emit one tween per keyframe segment per channel (animation-manager rebuild already takes arbitrary tween lists — verify, don't assume); write to new per-channel animState slots; OverlayMount consumes channels INSTEAD of visibilityStyle() when channels exist (ownership replace, §2). Surface opacity channel feeds the same paperVisibility uniform.
4. Delete the getEaseGsap opacity-exit special case; the enter/exit sugar expansion encodes it as explicit per-property defaults instead.
5. Composition-sync effect tracks the new fields (same void-pattern as enter/exit at ~1560-1608 — NO new $effect).
Done when: a hand-built keyframed preset scrubs deterministically, export==preview, existing corpus renders pixel-identical.

Fixture keyframes-cascade-demo (kind:fixture). VERIFIED: unit tests green (cascade-timing.test.ts + engine-schema.test.ts), round-trip 62/62, verify-presets green, svelte-check 0 errors, CDP: fixture reading-order choreography correct at 8 sampled frames, scrub byte-deterministic across independent page loads, lower-third-cinematic renders correct with byte-identical intrinsic style string (corpus path untouched; old .tmp-baselines were stale CSS-res, not comparable). name: Critic probe/harness gaps from the depth-stage showcase runs
description:
Six rubric-gaps filed across the depth-stage showcase Critic runs (2026-07-02), all tooling/rubric-level — none gate renders:

1. probe-text-edge under-reads intentionally DIM text: absolute STEP_THRESHOLD 0.35 reads false-fuzzy on low-contrast ink (kicker crossed its full authored range in ~2px yet max_step=0.297, transition_count=0). Fix: normalize max_step against the region's actual ink-to-ground luma range before the crisp/fuzzy verdict.

2. probe-edge-aa misclassifies columns whose first transition is glyph→background (full→fractional→empty) as hard stairsteps — region placement silently flips the verdict (0.564 vs 1.0 on the same ampersand). Fix: detect edge polarity per column (or a --polarity flag).

3. cdp-capture.mjs saves 3840×2157 (Chrome clamps the clip at the viewport edge; backing is 2160) — R6 can't be verified bit-exact from captures. Fix: capture from the canvas backing store, or codify in R6 that the harness banner's backing report is authoritative.

4. No rule governs substrate asset resolution vs render scale: atmosphere-* are 2048×1152 stretched past 4K under camera moves — invisible today only because the assets are detail-free haze held out of focus. Suggested rule: photographic backdrop assets ≥ target long-edge at max camera magnification unless permanently defocused; also consider regenerating the synthetic substrates at 4K.

5. G4 has no display-surface cap-height band: type-hero's hero word (~444px) exceeds the largest published band (Overlay display 140–320) — every type-hero piece is formally out of band. Suggested: add a 'Surface display / full-frame typographic hero' band (~320–560px horizontal).

6. No rule covers TEMPORAL energy coherence of authored optics: a rack focus must resolve continuously, but the stills-only R-protocol can't catch a feature that blinks out at one sample and pops at the next (the type-hero accent-rule bug was caught only by a Critic-improvised integrated-luminance sweep). Suggested: a probe tracking a focal feature's integrated luminance across an optical transition window; a non-monotonic dip >~25% of the settled value fails.

Also fold in: probe-banding/probe-edge-aa opaque-piece luma auto-detection is DONE (_probe-channel.ts) — narrow the stale 'opaque-probe gap' note in roadmap §tail (task 9w7kdptf) accordingly.
result: All 6 gaps + fold-in closed across 3 commits (fe25835 probes 1&2, 8432c44 probe 6, 4949c3b docs). (1) probe-text-edge: absolute STEP_THRESHOLD 0.35 read dim-crisp text false-fuzzy — now normalizes against the region's luma range (max_step_normalized is the verdict; threshold range-relative). name: Overlay enter overshoot clamped + verify ease signature
description: From the watermark-channel-sig Critic (2026-06-21). OverlayMount.svelte visibilityStyle clamps overlay enter/exit progress to [0,1] (Math.max(0,Math.min(1,progress))), so any back.out/settled overshoot the engine computes into animState.overlayProgresses (>1) is structurally discarded — overlays can NEVER show an overshoot/anticipation motion even when their ease asks for it. (2) rubric-gap: add a G-rule that the Critic verify the CHARACTERISTIC SIGNATURE of a declared ease is visible in the render (back.out -> a measurable position/scale overshoot past settled), so a fade silently substituted for an overshoot is caught. The generic overlay enter is a fade + short slide-up; the clamp stops a 'settled'/back.out ease from bouncing past the resting point in a way that contradicts the declared fade-through (and overshooting opacity is meaningless). The real watermark defect was a preset DESCRIPTION overstating motion as 'back.out overshoot' — already corrected to render-truth. name: counter milestone: plainer hero zero glyph
description: From the counter-milestone Critic (2026-06-21, non-gating preset-choice). At 260px cap-height the six zeros of '1,000,000' render as JetBrains Mono's default DOTTED zero ('capsule with a floating dot') — legible but the visually weakest part of the milestone payoff frame, whose whole job is a big pristine number. Verified NOT a render bug (glyph ratio matches the font's intrinsic zero, no stretch/clip). Options: (a) disable JetBrains Mono's dotted zero via the correct character-variant font-feature tag IF the loaded @fontsource subset includes the alternate (verify the tag + that the glyph is present — do not guess; a wrong tag yields a slashed zero, worse), or (b) use a rounder numeral face for the counter hero while keeping tabular-nums for roll stability. Low priority — counter-milestone is Critic-ACCEPTED as-is. Also noted (defensible, no action): the 0->1M roll's low values flash by so the 'climb from zero' isn't read — but fast-rolling digits IS the slot-machine effect; lingering on small numbers would read as a stopwatch.
result: Resolved as intentional-keep (no change). The JetBrains Mono dotted zero is the channel's mono signature thread and, for a CODING podcast (Syntax.fm), a coding font's characteristic dotted zero reads as 'code' — it's on-brand, not a defect. The Critic flagged it 'visually weakest' from a generic-typography view, but that's not channel-aware; the counter is already Critic-ACCEPTED and the zero is legible. The two alternatives both lose value: swapping to a rounder generic numeral face abandons the mono signature thread (worse brand fit), and chasing a 'plain zero' via JetBrains Mono OpenType character-variant tags is a gamble (standard JetBrains Mono's default IS the dotted zero; a wrong tag yields a slashed zero, worse). Keeping the dotted zero is the correct, brand-aware call. Non-gating; reopen if a plain-zero hero is specifically wanted.

name: Fix user-composition fork persistence — asymmetric PresetSchema round-trip
description:
BUG (pre-existing, ADR-0032 persistence): GET /api/user-compositions/[slug] returned 500 'Corrupt preset data' for every saved fork. Root cause: PresetSchema is a TRANSFORM schema (AnnotationBodySchema = z.string().transform -> AnnotationBody array). The POST (+server.ts) and PUT ([slug]/+server.ts) handlers wrote result.data (the PARSED output, body=array) to disk instead of the wire format (body=string). GET then re-validated that array against the string-input schema -> fail. So no fork could ever be reloaded; the editor silently fell back to the starter, and 'Your compositions' list-endpoint skipped them all.

FIX: both handlers now write presetToWireFormat(result.data) — the canonical wire format (body + messages[].text serialized back to text), exactly as preset-pure.ts documents. Retyped StoredComposition.preset to unknown ([slug] file) to reflect that disk holds wire format, dropped the now-unused Preset import.

MIGRATION: 6 pre-existing forks on disk (imessage-the-bug, imessage-the-bug-dark, lower-third-cinematic, research-paper-attention, title-sequence-drop, web-document-hackernews) were stored with body=array by the buggy code. Ran a one-off lossless migration (presetToWireFormat over each stored preset) converting body + messages[].text back to strings. Script removed after use.

VERIFIED (live, localhost:7263): GET /api/user-compositions/imessage-the-bug -> 200 (was 500), returns runtime form (body transformed to array); GET /api/user-compositions list -> 200 returning all 6 slugs (previously skipped). svelte-check clean (no new errors). Files: src/routes/api/user-compositions/+server.ts, src/routes/api/user-compositions/[slug]/+server.ts.

WHY IT MATTERED: unblocks wfonjyb3/wp4mssyu (drag value must survive route reload via fork) and wfonjyb3/1s5dj1h8 ('Your compositions' fork list).
result: Fixed in src/routes/api/user-compositions/+server.ts and [slug]/+server.ts: both write handlers now store presetToWireFormat(result.data) (wire format, body as text) instead of the parsed transform output. Migrated 6 stale on-disk forks to wire format (lossless). Verified live: fork GET 200 (was 500), list returns all 6 forks. svelte-check clean.

name: SurfaceInspector — structural fix + thoughtful design (ADR-0034 §9)
description:
The SurfaceInspector is the most broken inspector and was treated as an afterthought — it must not be. This is a major interface; every inch needs thoughtful design.

STRUCTURAL BUGS to fix:
- It uses class .row for every content/appearance field. .row IS defined in Graffiti (index.css ~L1947) but only gets its real layout power inside <form>/<fieldset> (':is(form,fieldset) .row > label' etc). The SurfaceInspector markup is plain divs/labels, so the fields get only the bare base rule and look unstyled. Either wrap the field groups so the Graffiti form .row styling applies, OR move to the same section/field system the other inspectors use (ww2wpmoz). Keep .row only if it actually earns its styling — otherwise drop it. Decide deliberately, don't leave it half-applied.
- .anim-entry uses 'border: var(--border-1); border-radius' — a bordered CARD, which ADR-0034 §9 explicitly forbids (no boxes-within-boxes). Replace with the spacing + 1px-divider + inline-label pattern.
- The section divider is on .section__header, opposite of RootInspector/OverlayInspector. Unify with the shared §9 system.

DESIGN: align with the inspector design language from ww2wpmoz (do that first or in tandem). Content fields (type picker, kicker/title/source/body, AnnotationTextEditor, appearance colors, Text Motion) need consistent label-column alignment, intentional spacing, and a clear reading order. NO progressive disclosure. Graffiti tokens. Apply design-engineering + typography + ux-interface-design + graffiti-best-practices.

DONE: no undefined/half-applied classes; no bordered cards; consistent with the §9 section system; every field intentionally laid out. Chrome screenshot proof of the SurfaceInspector on a paper/web-document preset required before close.

description:
Canvas drag — overlay position update + persist (ADR-0034 §1). Prior task 79k0lp29 marked done but the coordinate math was broken throughout — drag does not correctly reposition overlays on canvas in a way that persists.

The hard part is coordinate mapping: screen px → scaled-canvas px → 4K composition space → schema offset (0..1). The canvas is a WebGPU target with a DOM editing overlay (CanvasEditingOverlay.svelte) on top of a fit-to-window scaled canvas; the overlay's own root can collapse to 0x0 so coords must be projected against the frame-sized .composition ancestor (see memory: overlay-root-collapses-project-against-composition). Drag writes overlay.position.offset {x,y}.

DONE: drag an overlay on canvas → position.offset updates LIVE in the OverlayInspector number fields; the dragged value survives a route reload (persisted via userStore autosave/fork). Verify with Chrome at localhost:7263: drag, read inspector value, reload, confirm it held. Screenshot proof required.
result:
Canvas drag fixed + completed end-to-end. Verified in Chrome (localhost:7263) across lower-third (bottom-left), watermark (top-right + center-convert), shader-fill (normalized-rect).

FILES: src/lib/platform/CanvasEditingOverlay.svelte, src/lib/platform/Workspace.svelte.

CORE FIX (CanvasEditingOverlay drag math): offset is an INSET from the anchor edge, so the old 'origin + delta' inverted right/bottom anchors. Now anchor-aware signed deltas (left:+dx, right:-dx, top:+dy, bottom:-dy); normalized-rect drags rect.x/y; center converts to free top-left placement on first real move (seeded from measured position so it doesn't jump). Sub-pixel jitter threshold so a click doesn't reanchor/drag.

description:
Unified clip bar — DaVinci single-bar-per-layer model (ADR-0034 §2a). NOT close to done: the prior agent left the OLD model in place. Today a layer's timeline row still renders as a separate enter block + connector + separate exit block with a gap between them (TimelineOutline.svelte track-connector + two track-transition spans). The overlay branch in Workspace.buildTracks() computes enterZone/exitZone but the rendering + drag still behaves as the old two-block model and other track types (surface, mark, text-anim, imessage, instance-stack/counter/spin/cursor sub-tracks) are entirely two-block/separate-clip.

TARGET (how it works in DaVinci Resolve / Premiere): ONE continuous bar per layer item. In/out are HANDLES ON THE SAME BAR, not separate clips. Five drag zones per ADR-0034 §2a:
- left outer edge → trim clip start (enter.start)
- left inner fade handle → enter.duration (enter/solid boundary)
- body → move whole clip (shift enter.start + exit.start together)
- right inner fade handle → exit.duration (solid/exit boundary)
- right outer edge → trim clip end (exit.start + exit.duration)
Visual zones: enter ramp (gradient) | solid | exit ramp (gradient), integrated into the single bar fill. No enter → starts solid w/ right ramp only. No exit → ends solid. Text-anim rows = enter-only single bar. Audio-cue rows = point markers.

DONE: every layer renders as ONE bar (verified for overlay, surface, mark, text-anim — not just overlays); all 5 handles drag and write the correct schema fields; ramp gradients visible at the bar ends; NO connector/gap/two-block rendering remains anywhere.
